title: join a planning thread live in the terminal
goal: 'autonomouse plan join <thread-id>' marks the thread human_joined, runs 'claude --resume <session_id>' interactively in the repository directory so the human continues the same conversation with the same context, and on exit marks the thread waiting_planner (or closed if the planner closed it) so unattended resumes continue; while a thread is human_joined, 'plan step' skips it. 'autonomouse plan new <project>' starts an interactive planner session from scratch and records the thread the same way. The screen shows the join command on a thread.
limits: Never two resumes of one session at once: the human_joined mark is a claim with pid and liveness like a project claim
test: Open a thread on a temp board, 'plan join' it with a fake claude that records its argv: argv contains --resume and the thread's session id, the thread is human_joined with the pid while it runs, and waiting_planner after; 'plan step' during the join leaves the thread alone. One live join on the real board, confirmed by the human. uv run pytest -q and uv run ruff check pass.
